timeline.message:
Fix ByteBufUtil indexOf ClassCastException

Signed-off-by: xingrufei <xingrufei@sogou-inc.com>
timeline.author: xingrufei

timeline.body:
Motivation:

In this issue(https://github.com/netty/netty/issues/11678) , it is proposed that `ByteBufUtil.indexOf()` may throw `ClassCastException`, so type checking on `haystack` is required

Modification:

Use `ByteBuf.indexOf()` instead of `firstIndexOf()`, and add test case

Result:

Fixes https://github.com/netty/netty/issues/11678

timeline.author: skyguard1

timeline.body: This comment is not correct anymore... Should it be : `the firstIndexOf method can be used` ?

timeline.author: xingrufei
xingrufei

timeline.body:
You can use the `ByteBuf.indexOf(int fromIndex, int toIndex, byte value)` method instead. When the buffer is an `AbstractByteBuf` this will delegate to `firstIndexOf`.

Then the shortcut won't be skipped for other buffer implementations.

timeline.message:
Use ByteBuf.indexOf() when haystack is not AbstractByteBuf

Signed-off-by: xingrufei <xingrufei@sogou-inc.com>
timeline.author: xingrufei

timeline.body: Sorry, I meant instead of doing the `instanceof` check, we can just always call `haystack.indexOf(haystack.readerIndex(), haystack.writerIndex(), needle.getByte(needle.readerIndex()))`
Also, I think we can simplify this ternary operation so it's easier to read.

timeline.message:
